headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Khoj’s retrieved notes feed Windsurf’s tool-using editor loop.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can perform RAG plus optional web search, while Windsurf can ingest files, clipboard, and MCP outputs in a tool-using editor loop. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge even without a documented direct channel. The shared path is not provably blocked, so I rate it medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Khoj output is copied into Windsurf chat, clipboard, or an MCP-fed file
IF Windsurf treats retrieved note text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of retrieved notes into Windsurf
Use a read-only export folder for Khoj outputs
Add a prompt-injection warning banner before pasting notes
Restrict Windsurf MCP servers to trusted, allowlisted sources
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging from Khoj into downstream prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, and Windsurf touches source code and open files. Windsurf’s shared state is via local filesystem, so if both are pointed at the same workspace or export directory, sensitive note content can flow into the coding agent’s context. Khoj’s broad egress and Windsurf’s model proxy/MCP paths increase exposure, though not enough for high without a documented shared workspace.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to read the same local directory
IF Khoj indexes files that Windsurf can also open or upload
mitigations: Separate note and code workspaces on disk
Exclude personal-note directories from Windsurf indexing
Review Windsurf MCP/server destinations before use
Keep Khoj self-hosted with restricted outbound access
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory ACLs or sandbox mounts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Khoj reads files and maintains a shared index across the user’s clients. If both operate on the same repository or workspace, Windsurf’s writes can race with Khoj’s indexing and stale retrieval, causing conflicting edits and broken state. The overlap is dangerous by default once they share a workspace, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes a directory that Windsurf edits
IF Windsurf auto-executes file or git changes in the same workspace
mitigations: Use separate repos for notes and code
Pause Khoj reindexing during large Windsurf refactors
Require manual git review before Windsurf commits
Turn off Windsurf auto-execute unless needed
requires-engineering: add file-locking or workspace lease coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can surface retrieved facts from personal notes and documents, and Windsurf’s Cascade loop can act on file and tool outputs. If Windsurf treats Khoj’s retrieved text as authoritative, a mistaken or injected note can cascade into code changes, commits, or terminal actions. Because Windsurf has execution authority and Khoj is a retrieval agent, the downstream blast radius is high.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses Khoj output as a source of truth without verification
IF Windsurf auto-applies edits or commands derived from retrieved notes
mitigations: Require human verification before applying Khoj-derived changes
Ask Windsurf to cite original source files before acting
Disable auto-execute for tasks sourced from notes
Limit Khoj outputs to summaries, not directives
requires-engineering: add verification gates between retrieval and action

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj is self-hostable and handles personal notes, while Windsurf is a closed-source editor agent with broad egress and model-proxy/MCP paths. If personal notes or regulated documents are moved from a self-hosted Khoj deployment into Windsurf, retention and residency controls may diverge. I cite both because the mismatch arises only when data flows between them.
conditions: IF regulated notes or documents are opened in Windsurf after being retrieved by Khoj
IF the two products have different retention or residency settings for the same data class
mitigations: Keep regulated documents only in the self-hosted Khoj environment
Review Windsurf retention and telemetry settings
Avoid pasting personal notes into Windsurf prompts
Document a data-flow policy for note-to-code transfers
requires-engineering: add DPA/residency controls for cross-tool transfers
